welcome.title: Welcome to Seredina!
welcome.body: A quick look at where everything lives. You can skip this tour at any time.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.body: This is where you land every time you log in — widgets for ticket volume, SLA, and more, which you can hide or reorder.

checklist.title: Get started
checklist.body: This checklist walks you through setting up your organization: customizing ticket statuses, an SLA policy, a macro, and inviting your team.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.body: Everything that comes in — by email, the API, or a monitoring alert — ends up as a ticket here.

processes.title: Processes
processes.body: Reusable checklists on top of a ticket: onboarding, changes, releases.

knowledgeBase.title: Knowledge Base

emailChannels.title: Email Channels
emailChannels.intro: Tickets are created from the mail that arrives in these mailboxes; agent replies go back out through the same account. Connect Microsoft 365 or Gmail with OAuth, or any other provider with IMAP/SMTP.
emailChannels.name: Name
emailChannels.connectedNotice: Mailbox connected. New mail will start arriving as tickets within a minute.
emailChannels.mailboxAddress: Mailbox address (the account you'll sign in with)

microsoft_oauth.title: Before you start: register an app in Microsoft Entra
microsoft_oauth.steps: In the Azure portal go to Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. Add the redirect URI below as a "Web" platform. Under API permissions add the Office 365 Exchange Online delegated permissions IMAP.AccessAsUser.All and SMTP.Send (plus offline_access), then grant admin consent. Create a client secret under Certificates & secrets. SMTP AUTH must be enabled for the mailbox.

google_oauth.title: Before you start: create an OAuth client in Google Cloud
google_oauth.steps: In the Google Cloud console enable the Gmail API, configure the OAuth consent screen (Internal for Workspace), and add the https://mail.google.com/ scope. Then create Credentials → OAuth client ID of type "Web application" and add the redirect URI below.

emailChannels.redirectUriMissing: The server has no public address configured (WEB_ORIGIN or API_PUBLIC_URL), so the provider can't send you back here.

setupRequired.title: Set up two-factor sign-in
setupRequired.subtitle: Your workspace requires a code from an authenticator app at every sign-in. It takes a minute.

enroll.step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…).
enroll.step2: In the app, add an account and scan this QR code.
enroll.step3: Type the 6-digit code the app shows.
enroll.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
enroll.cantScan: Can't scan it? Enter this key by hand

recovery.title: Save your recovery codes
recovery.explain: If you lose your phone, each of these codes lets you sign in once. Keep them somewhere safe, like a password manager. They won't be shown again.

accountSecurity.intro: Protect your account with a second step at sign-in: a code from an authenticator app on your phone.

mfa.policyOff: Optional: each user decides in Account security.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.intro: Let people sign in with their Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or other OpenID Connect account instead of a separate Seredina password. Two-factor sign-in is then up to your identity provider.
sso.loadFailed: Failed to load single sign-on settings
sso.saved: Saved. Try it from the sign-in page in a private window before requiring it.
sso.confirmRemove: Remove single sign-on? Everyone goes back to signing in with a password.

setup.microsoft: In the Azure portal: Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration, single tenant, redirect URI of type "Web" = the URI below. Create a client secret under Certificates & secrets. Copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
setup.google: In the Google Cloud console: configure the OAuth consent screen (Internal), then Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application, with the redirect URI below.
setup.oidc: Register a confidential "web" client in your identity provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Okta, Auth0…) with the redirect URI below and the scopes openid, email and profile. The issuer URL is the one whose /.well-known/openid-configuration the provider publishes.

sso.redirectUriMissing: The server has no public address configured (WEB_ORIGIN or API_PUBLIC_URL).
sso.clientSecretKeep: Client secret (leave empty to keep the saved one)
sso.autoProvisionHint: The first time someone from an allowed domain signs in, give them an account with the role below. Otherwise an admin must add them on the Users page first.
sso.enabledHint: Adds a "Sign in with SSO" button to the sign-in page. Passwords keep working.
sso.enforcedHint: Only admins can still sign in with a password — the way back in if the identity provider has a problem.

aiTriage.title: AI triage of new tickets
aiTriage.intro: When a ticket comes in, the AI reads its subject and first message and picks a priority and a team. Each new ticket costs one small model call.

suggest.label: Suggest
suggest.hint: Show the suggestion on the ticket; an agent applies it with one click.

auto.label: Apply automatically
auto.hint: Set the priority and team right away — only if nobody set them already — and leave an internal note explaining why.
